newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgrade strife seen topping Contact Group agenda.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade strife seen topping Contact Group agenda.

text.p: The Contact Group on former Yugoslavia will meet in Brussels on Saturday amid expectations the five nations will seek to find a common stance on Serbia.
U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Europe John Kornblum was to arrive in the Belgian capital late on Friday evening after consultations in the Netherlands with the Dutch European Union presidency.

NATO sources said the Contact Group meeting was part of the regular cycle of talks between the five nations -- the United States, Britain, Germany, France and Russia -- but that the situation in Belgrade was likely to top the agenda.
"I have the impression that they are going to try to get a unified position," one NATO source said. "They will probably come out with a fairly strong statement."
Friday marked the 53rd day of mass demonstrations in Serbia against the annulment by President Slobodan Milosevic's government of opposition victories in November local elections.
The European Union has called in a statement released on Thursday night for Milosevic to accept the opposition poll victories and for Serbia to embrace democracy and human rights.
